quest.title: This Ain't Your Daddy's Iridescence Tour...
quest.description: You've received an invitation from one Arataki Itto. Having been introduced by his enthusiastic letter, you set out on a trip to Watatsumi Island...
quest.rewards_formatted: Primogem x30, Iridescence Tour Tickets x80, Mora x50000, Hero's Wit x5

chapter.num: Iridescent Arataki Rockin' for Life Tour de Force of Awesomeness: First Leg
chapter.title: This Ain't Your Daddy's Iridescence Tour...

dialogues.speaker: Dvorak
dialogues.text: Feel free to take a look around, I'll be with you in just a moment.

dialogues.speaker: Arataki Itto
dialogues.text: Don't you worry, Jack-Attack! We'll find that dog, even if it's hiding in Tenshukaku.

dialogues.speaker: Dvorak
dialogues.text: Itto... It's just a myth...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: What dog?

dialogues.speaker: Arataki Itto
dialogues.text: Whoa! Compadre! And Paimon!

dialogues.speaker: Arataki Itto
dialogues.text: You finally made it! Man, have I missed you guys! Hahahahaha!

dialogues.speaker: Arataki Itto
dialogues.text: Oh yeah — and this is Dvorak, a musician from Fontaine. Jack-Attack, you know these two, right?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hey! Mr. Dvorak! It's you!

dialogues.speaker: Dvorak
dialogues.text: Hehe, ah, it's so wonderful to see you both again. I feel like that Lantern Rite was just yesterday. How've you been?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Pretty good! So how did you end up hanging around with Itto? Is he helping you with the Iridescence Tour now?

dialogues.speaker: Arataki Itto
dialogues.text: You'd better believe it, Mini Melon! But that's only half the story.

dialogues.speaker: Arataki Itto
dialogues.text: This is no ordinary Iridescence Tour. Me and Jack-Attack are teaming up to turn this into the "Iridescent Arataki Rockin' for Life Tour de Force of Awesomeness"!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Rockin' for Life? What do you know about rock 'n' roll, Bull-Chucker?

dialogues.speaker: Arataki Itto
dialogues.text: Huh? What, you never heard of Bull-Chucker Rock before?

dialogues.speaker: Arataki Itto
dialogues.text: Moo moo moo... *stomp stomp stomp*

dialogues.speaker: Arataki Itto
dialogues.text: Don't try and understand it, Mini Melon, it'll melt your mind! It's about lettin' loose! C'mon, give us some Lavender Melon Rock!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Okay, speak for yourself, mister... Sounds like you're the one whose mind is melting!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Just to backtrack a little — what's this dog you were talking about?

dialogues.speaker: Dvorak
dialogues.text: Heh... Just a local legend I heard about. Apparently, there was a war between the islands of Narukami and Watatsumi not too long ago. Is that right?

dialogues.speaker: Arataki Itto
dialogues.text: Such a waste... When will people learn? Make rock 'n' roll, guys, not war.

dialogues.speaker: Dvorak
dialogues.text: A tragedy, to be sure. Countless animals were affected by the fallout. A raven, a bake-danuki, a weasel thief, and many more sustained injuries...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Um... Fair point, the animals didn't deserve that. But, uh... And not to downplay it or anything but... Didn't even worse stuff happen than that?

dialogues.speaker: Arataki Itto
dialogues.text: In the eyes of a rocker, all living things are equally important.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: So did this dog get injured, too?

dialogues.speaker: Dvorak
dialogues.text: No, the story goes that this dog was something like a ninken. It would show up out of nowhere in the middle of a battle to rescue the injured animals and take them to safety.

dialogues.speaker: Arataki Itto
dialogues.text: Rockin' and rollin' to the rescue! A king among canines! There'll always be a place for him in the Arataki Gang.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Where did you hear about this?

dialogues.speaker: Dvorak
dialogues.text: In Ritou. I was actually there while the war was going on.

dialogues.speaker: Dvorak
dialogues.text: It inspired me to write a song about it. I was even planning to host a music festival around the same theme, but unfortunately I couldn't convince my investors.

dialogues.speaker: Arataki Itto
dialogues.text: Oh, yeah, I heard all about that... They claimed that they had to cancel their plans because of an accident at sea. But that was just a lame excuse.

dialogues.speaker: Dvorak
dialogues.text: Yes, they weren't optimistic about the potential return on investment. Plus... I don't know, there seemed to be some other risks they were worried about.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: What kind of risks?

dialogues.speaker: Dvorak
dialogues.text: Good question... Risks only apparent to people with Mora to throw around, I suppose?

dialogues.speaker: Arataki Itto
dialogues.text: I agree. When people have too much Mora, they lose their rock 'n' roll spirit.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: They do, huh? So what do you mean by rock 'n' roll spirit, anyway?

dialogues.speaker: Arataki Itto
dialogues.text: Y'know! The spirit of, uh... You rock up, you rock out, roll the dice, and roll with the punches! That sorta stuff!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh... By that definition, aren't the investors the most rock 'n' roll people in this scenario?

dialogues.speaker: Arataki Itto
dialogues.text: Anyway, point is — those chumps are out, and Arataki Itto is in! I'm running the show from here on out.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Yeah, right! How are YOU gonna fill in for the investors? Do you even have any Mora?

dialogues.speaker: Dvorak
dialogues.text: I have faith in Itto. He tells me that the Arataki Gang is a small but well-known and influential organization in this area, and has even been known to rub shoulders with the local authorities. Isn't that right?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: "Rub shoulders" is putting it mildly... More like, they're always locking horns...

dialogues.speaker: Arataki Itto
dialogues.text: Hey! Don't look down your nose at the Arataki Gang! I got connections, alright? Even the Tri-Commission listens to what I have to say!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Okay, Mr. Big Shot, whatever you say...

dialogues.speaker: Arataki Itto
dialogues.text: You can doubt it all you want, Mini Melon, but it's the truth. You know that guy in the Yashiro Commission? Well, he and I are officially bros! That's right, I'm talking about Thoma, housekeeper extraordinaire!

dialogues.speaker: Arataki Itto
dialogues.text: And there's the general from the Tenryou Commission. Kujou Tengu. I mean, sure, we're always ribbing each other, but it comes from a place of deep mutual respect!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Mutual? ...Yeah, Paimon's not so sure about that.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: So what about the Kanjou Commission?

dialogues.speaker: Arataki Itto
dialogues.text: Okay, fair, no first-name contacts there... But the Arataki Gang is a big contributor to their revenue stream! All those fines we pay...

dialogues.speaker: Dvorak
dialogues.text: F—Fines!?

dialogues.speaker: Arataki Itto
dialogues.text: Huh? No! I meant, uh... taxes! Hehehe... Yeah...

dialogues.speaker: Arataki Itto
dialogues.text: But that's not all! Let's not forget my contacts outside of the Tri-Commission! Amazing, talented people from all walks of life, like, uh... Ooh! Like the TCG legend, Ayato! Oh yeah, he's made quite a name for himself in the TCG circles.

dialogues.speaker: Arataki Itto
dialogues.text: In fact, they got a saying now: "Ayato of the South, Itto of the North." That's right, I'm the only serious competition he's got in all of Inazuma!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Did you make that saying up!?

dialogues.speaker: Arataki Itto
dialogues.text: Then there's the fox lady, VIP customer of Yukio's ramen stall and fellow participant in the Ramen Masters Championship. I was her only worthy opponent.

dialogues.speaker: Arataki Itto
dialogues.text: Also, you know that lonely god in Tenshukaku? Well, guess what? Turns out it was her life-long wish to catch one of Arataki Itto's events!

dialogues.speaker: Arataki Itto
dialogues.text: During the Drumalong festival, the Tenryou Commission were worried that their Almighty Shogun might have too much fun and lose interest in running the government. That's why they invited me over to stay for a couple of days.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Well look at you, sounds like you're really going up in the world. At this rate, you'll have made shogun by the next time we see you... And then Paimon'll have to call you "Almighty Bull-Chucker."

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: The Arataki Gang never ceases to amaze.

dialogues.speaker: Dvorak
dialogues.text: Ahem, well... I'll admit, I heard a few exaggerations there myself, but regardless, Itto has helped me secure a venue for this event. And for that, I owe him my thanks.

dialogues.speaker: Arataki Itto
dialogues.text: Ah, it's nothing, don't mention it! My bro Gorou sorted it all out for me — let's both go thank him later.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wait, you know Gorou!?

dialogues.speaker: Arataki Itto
dialogues.text: Yep. I always knew him as General Gorou of the resistance fighters, but I had no idea there was more to the story! Turns out, he has another identity...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: What other identity?

dialogues.speaker: Arataki Itto
dialogues.text: You've heard of Ms. Hina, right?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: MS. HINA!? So you—!

dialogues.speaker: Arataki Itto
dialogues.text: Hey, no need to yell, alright? Yes, Ms. Hina. She's the one who told me.

dialogues.speaker: Arataki Itto
dialogues.text: After falling for the Tenryou Commission's tricks at the Drumalong Festival, I figured I'd find a new location this time. Somewhere out of their reach. Like here, for example.

dialogues.speaker: Arataki Itto
dialogues.text: So, I wrote Ms. Hina a letter, asking if she knew anything about the procedure for holding an event on Watatsumi Island.

dialogues.speaker: Arataki Itto
dialogues.text: She wrote me back right away, and said I could ask Watatsumi Island's General for help... and that his name was "Gorou."

dialogues.speaker: Arataki Itto
dialogues.text: I was like, whaaaat!? General Gorou is the general of all Watatsumi Island!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Whew, that was close... Paimon's with you now, but... what did you think general meant?

dialogues.speaker: Arataki Itto
dialogues.text: What do you mean? Isn't it like, one general per squad, or something?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: That's called a captain!

dialogues.speaker: Arataki Itto
dialogues.text: Really? Huh. Well, either way, if it wasn't for Ms. Hina, I never woulda known... Pretty rock 'n' roll! Hahahahaha!

response.speaker: Arataki Itto
response.text: Alright — good chat, compadre. I just remembered, I got a meeting with Gorou coming up — gonna ask him about that dog situation. Gonna have to love ya and leave ya for now.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Sure you don't want us to join? We could help.

response.speaker: Arataki Itto
response.text: Hahahahaha! You guys focus on having a blast here at the festival! I think I can handle this little canine conundrum.

response.speaker: Arataki Itto
response.text: There's still a few days until the big party, so not everything's set up yet. But the Jam Zone and the Roasted Lavender Melon Zone are ready for action!

response.speaker: Dvorak
response.text: *sigh* What a character... Gotta admire his enthusiasm, though.

response.speaker: Dvorak
response.text: Looks like it's just the three of us for now. Why don't I show you the Jam Zone to start with?

dialogues.speaker: Dvorak
dialogues.text: Here we are. I've supplied musical scores and instruments from various regions, including a horn I personally brought from Fontaine. You can play whatever music you like.

dialogues.speaker: Dvorak
dialogues.text: If you get tired, the Roasted Lavender Melon Zone is just over there. Itto says that Lavender Melons are, *clears throat*, rock 'n' roll fuel. So, what do you think? Wanna give it a try?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: I guess that makes Paimon "Flying Rock 'N' Roll Fuel."

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hey, cut that out! Lucky Itto's gone, otherwise Paimon would never hear the end of it.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Let's change the topic. What other fun stuff is there to do here, Mr. Dvorak?

dialogues.speaker: Dvorak
dialogues.text: Well, we're planning to invite some more music enthusiasts, and we're still getting some supplies together so we can decorate the place a little.

dialogues.speaker: Dvorak
dialogues.text: But it could take some time. The Arataki Gang has shifted their focus to the dog situation ever since I brought it up...

dialogues.speaker: Dvorak
dialogues.text: Only one of them is actually sticking to the plan. Her name is Kuki Shinobu — she's out delivering invitations right now.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Yep, that's the Arataki Gang for ya. Everyone else goofs around while Shinobu gets things done.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: We should help out! We can't let this event get totally derailed when Shinobu's out there doing her part!

dialogues.speaker: Dvorak
dialogues.text: Oh, I mean... Are you sure?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Absolutely. We can handle it.

dialogues.speaker: Dvorak
dialogues.text: That would be extremely useful... We're starting to get behind schedule, and a couple extra pairs of hands could make all the difference.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: No problem, we're happy to help! So you need us to find some music lovers and gather materials for decorating. Was that it?

dialogues.speaker: Dvorak
dialogues.text: Exactly. According to the original plan, we aim to finish everything in five days, and then the big party can begin.

dialogues.speaker: Dvorak
dialogues.text: Actually, give me a second — I'll make you a checklist of all the outstanding tasks, that way it'll all be clearer.

dialogues.speaker: Dvorak
dialogues.text: Oh, also... One other tidbit to share with you: Itto is planning to perform a song on stage on the final day of the event.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ugh, typical Bull-Chucker! Always has to be the center of attention!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Why don't you do a song too, Paimon?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh, Paimon would steal the show for sure. No one would give Itto a second look after that.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Pretty sure he'd yell out "Paimon's so rock 'n' roll it hurts!" And then run off the stage bawling his eyes out.

dialogues.speaker: Dvorak
dialogues.text: Haha, those are some bold claims, Ms. Paimon. But that kind of confidence would serve you well on the stage.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ah, Paimon's just kidding. Anyway, we'll be ready for that checklist as soon as it's done, Mr. Dvorak!

dialogues.speaker: Dvorak
dialogues.text: Great. Feel free to take a look around. I'll bring it over in a few minutes.

dialogues.speaker: Shikanoin Heizou
dialogues.text: #Well, well, well! If it isn't {NICKNAME} and Paimon!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Whoa! Shinobu... and Heizou! What a surprise!

dialogues.speaker: Shikanoin Heizou
dialogues.text: This truly is a pleasant surprise... although, not that surprising to be honest. I was just telling Ms. Shinobu that I had a sneaking suspicion we might run into you.

dialogues.speaker: Kuki Shinobu
dialogues.text: Hehe, Doushin Shikanoin was talking about you constantly the whole way here. I guess the universe answered his prayers.

dialogues.speaker: Shikanoin Heizou
dialogues.text: It's called intuition. Names pop into my head at relevant moments — just the way my mind works.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: It's great to see you both.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Paimon sure wasn't expecting Heizou to be the first one to show up.

dialogues.speaker: Kuki Shinobu
dialogues.text: Boss nagged me to prioritize the Tenryou Commission invitations. He specifically requested Madam Kujou Sara and Doushin Shikanoin.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So... why isn't Sara here?

dialogues.speaker: Shikanoin Heizou
dialogues.text: Almost certainly because she has no desire whatsoever to see Itto. In her defense, here's what was written on the invitation letter:

dialogues.speaker: Shikanoin Heizou
dialogues.text: "Kujou Tengu! Come meet me at the top of the Sangonomiya Shrine! Let's go nuts and have a totally rock 'n' roll sumo wrestling match!"

dialogues.speaker: Kuki Shinobu
dialogues.text: If I were Kujou Sara, I'd jump at the chance to throw Itto off the roof.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: But then wouldn't Kokomi come and throw Sara off, too? All that stomping around on her roof... the noise would drive her crazy.

dialogues.speaker: Kuki Shinobu
dialogues.text: Yeah, haha... Well anyway, Madam Kujou Sara's response was much more magnanimous than mine would've been. She gave us a basket of Lavender Melons to bring as a gift.

dialogues.speaker: Shikanoin Heizou
dialogues.text: Magnanimous...? Hehe, I'm not so sure. Something tells me she's trying to send a message.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: What message?

dialogues.speaker: Shikanoin Heizou
dialogues.text: "If that oni brat wants to pick a fight with me, there'll be plenty of Lavender Melons waiting for him at the Police Station."

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hm, maybe the fact you assume that says more about you than her! So what about the other basket of Lavender Melons, huh? Is that one from you? What message are you trying to send?

dialogues.speaker: Shikanoin Heizou
dialogues.text: Haha, the other basket is actually from a few of us at the Police Station. I chipped in, and so did some other Doushin who've arrested Itto before... and so did some of Itto's former cellmates.

dialogues.speaker: Shikanoin Heizou
dialogues.text: So I guess this basket of Lavender Melons is our way of saying: "There'll always be a place for you here!"

dialogues.speaker: Kuki Shinobu
dialogues.text: Maybe just give Boss the melons, and don't mention that part.

dialogues.speaker: Shikanoin Heizou
dialogues.text: #Sure. Well, my work here is done, anyway. Now that I've delivered the Lavender Melons and said hello to {NICKNAME}, I should probably get going.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Uh, aren't you gonna stay for the event?

dialogues.speaker: Shikanoin Heizou
dialogues.text: Don't worry, I'll definitely be back for the big party. But I have some business to attend to in Ritou first.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Yeesh, being a detective sounds busy. They got you running around all over the place... Oh, wait! Ritou! Do you happen to know anything about a mystery ninken that appeared during the war? Apparently, a lot of people in Ritou were talking about it.

dialogues.speaker: Shikanoin Heizou
dialogues.text: Ah, the dog, yes...? That was the inspiration behind this music festival, wasn't it? Shinobu told me all about it.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh... Never mind, Paimon just thought a detective might have the inside scoop.

dialogues.speaker: Shikanoin Heizou
dialogues.text: I'm only speculating here, but from experience, I'd say it's probably just a local legend. I doubt the dog even exists.

dialogues.speaker: Shikanoin Heizou
dialogues.text: What's wrong? From the look on your face, you've got a vested interest in this situation...

dialogues.speaker: Shikanoin Heizou
dialogues.text: Interesting... Well, since I'm going to Ritou anyway, I can always ask around and see where it leads.

choices.text: Are you sure it won't impact your work?

response.speaker: Shikanoin Heizou
response.text: Don't be silly. If this matters to you, that's a good sign that it'll turn out to be something that interests me, too.

response.speaker: Shikanoin Heizou
response.text: Hehe, stay tuned for more info. See you all soon!

response.speaker: Kuki Shinobu
response.text: Seems like Doushin Shikanoin's quite the lone wolf. Well, I'd better get back to delivering these invitations. Gotta make sure the big party's a success.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: In that case, guess it's time for us to get to work too. Wonder how that checklist is coming along...

response.speaker: Dvorak
response.text: Sorry to keep you waiting — here's that list for ya. If you can work your way through all this, we'll be back on track.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Great, perfect timing, Mr. Dvorak! We'll get on it right away.

response.speaker: Dvorak
response.text: Thank you, I'm very grateful for your help. If you feel like flexing your musical muscles to take a break at any point, just come and find me in the Jam Zone.

choices.text: How much do you charge for your services?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: I'd like to buy some antiques.

dialogues.speaker: Linlang
dialogues.text: Yes, please browse as you like. You'll find that our antiques here are worth every Mora.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Goodbye.

dialogues.speaker: Linlang
dialogues.text: Goodbye. Come back any time.

dialogues.speaker: Xingxi
dialogues.text: Ah, now that brings back memories! It reminds me of how when I was young, I would wake up very early to attend calligraphy classes at my teacher's place. It was so early that it was still dark outside, and it was terribly frightening.

dialogues.speaker: Xingxi
dialogues.text: Fortunately, I would pass by the house of an old granny, and I could often hear this song drifting out from her home. It would give me a sense of peace.

dialogues.speaker: Xingxi
dialogues.text: That dear old lady probably isn't with us anymore, but I've also grown, and I'm no longer as afraid of the dark, haha...

dialogues.speaker: Xingxi
dialogues.text: In any case, I've given it some serious consideration, and while I'd love to agree, it's going to be tough finding someone to watch a time-honored store like ours on such short notice.

dialogues.speaker: Xingxi
dialogues.text: So let me recommend someone else to you who might attend instead — Xigu Antiques's boss, Linlang.

dialogues.speaker: Xingxi
dialogues.text: She doesn't even open in the daytime, and you can either find her sleeping or wandering the streets — I reckon she'd have the free time to help.

dialogues.speaker: Xingxi
dialogues.text: Regardless, thank you so much for letting me hear that song again. I hope your musical venture goes well!

dialogues.speaker: Linlang
dialogues.text: My dear guest, it would be no exaggeration to compare your performance to an adeptal hymn.

dialogues.speaker: Linlang
dialogues.text: When I was just starting in this line of work, I went to Minlin to purchase some ancient jade. On the way there, I heard music coming from Qingyun Peak.

dialogues.speaker: Linlang
dialogues.text: I was so enraptured that I wondered if it might be the music of the adepti themselves, you know? Haha. Thank you — I thought I'd never get the opportunity to hear it again.

dialogues.speaker: Linlang
dialogues.text: As for the music festival, I must say that I wouldn't call myself any kind of music enthusiast — I simply happen to like this tune. So forgive me if I must decline.

dialogues.speaker: Linlang
dialogues.text: But allow me to let slip from my lips this tidbit of gossip: I believe Mingxing Jewelry's boss, Xingxi, is a closet fan of music. Perhaps you could ask her?

dialogues.speaker: Linlang
dialogues.text: Last but not least, I wish you the best of luck with your festival.

dialogues.speaker: Jifang
dialogues.text: What a wonderfully nostalgic feeling. I was immediately reminded of my studies in Fontaine.

dialogues.speaker: Jifang
dialogues.text: I would often go to cafes in Vasari Passage to read, and when I heard this song one day, I asked the barista what it was called.

dialogues.speaker: Jifang
dialogues.text: They didn't know, but a large fellow having some cake nearby told me that it was named "Le Souvenir avec le crepuscule." And yeah, later on, he became my husband.

dialogues.speaker: Jifang
dialogues.text: He was at the cafe meeting with his friends from a literary club back then. Ah, how nostalgic. We were all so young!

dialogues.speaker: Jifang
dialogues.text: Oh, right! Your music festival... I fear I shan't be able to attend, but if needed, I can get my husband to go.

dialogues.speaker: Jifang
dialogues.text: He's been fiddling with some old books that haven't been selling well all day, and I haven't been able to dissuade him from doing so.

dialogues.speaker: Jifang
dialogues.text: But I'm sure such cultural exchanges would interest him. I'll ask him to bring some souvenirs along that he can give out to boot.

dialogues.speaker: Marjorie
dialogues.text: This tune is so gentle, just the way I remember it.

dialogues.speaker: Marjorie
dialogues.text: My dad used to play this one for me on his harmonica while we were on the way back from Springvale.

dialogues.speaker: Marjorie
dialogues.text: He said that this tune represented Springvale itself, and that's where Dad's dad grew up.

dialogues.speaker: Marjorie
dialogues.text: Shame that my grandfather would pass before I was ever born.

dialogues.speaker: Marjorie
dialogues.text: Thanks for playing that music. You know what? I've decided that I should spend a bit more time with my dad. He's an adventurer, so he tends to spend time out in the field.

dialogues.speaker: Marjorie
dialogues.text: So, if you don't mind, I might have to give this festival a pass, but if there's another opportunity, I'll come — and drag him along as well!

dialogues.speaker: Flora
dialogues.text: Ooh, you're great! This is even better than when Mr. Sayid plays it! He performed this one for us last Windblume Festival, saying that it was a traditional song from Sumeru.

dialogues.speaker: Flora
dialogues.text: Donna said it sounded terrible compared to Master Diluc's playing, though.

dialogues.speaker: Flora
dialogues.text: Well, I've made up my mind. The flowers need care every day, and Inazuma's pretty far away, so I'm afraid I can't go.

dialogues.speaker: Flora
dialogues.text: Thanks for the music, though. It was lovely. On that note, I'll offer you a special price if you need flowers for your festival!

dialogues.speaker: Charles
dialogues.text: Very impressive. In fact, I should recommend to Adelinde that you be commissioned to play at the next such family event.

dialogues.speaker: Charles
dialogues.text: As for your invitation... To be honest, I was just about ready to agree the moment you finished your performance.

dialogues.speaker: Charles
dialogues.text: But I'm not sure if I'd want to ask Master Diluc for a day off over something this trivial — after all, he'd agree without hesitation.

dialogues.speaker: Charles
dialogues.text: How about this, then? I'll send you a token of support for your festival. Will that do?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: So you'll be sending us several crates of wine?

dialogues.speaker: Charles
dialogues.text: Haha, I doubt everyone who'll be attending the festival will be of drinking age.

dialogues.speaker: Charles
dialogues.text: As such, I'll give you some decorative banners instead. We've got them stocked in the winery warehouse — and I believe they'll come in quite handy.

dialogues.speaker: Charles
dialogues.text: Don't worry, you won't have to go fetch them yourselves. I'll have some of our traders deliver it directly.

dialogues.speaker: Charles
dialogues.text: Just consider it the "Angel's Share."

dialogues.speaker: Aoi
dialogues.text: Ah... Lovely. It seems you're quite the dab hand at making others' wishes come true.

dialogues.speaker: Aoi
dialogues.text: It's been almost twenty years since I last heard this tune. It was a boy in the neighborhood who played it for me.

dialogues.speaker: Aoi
dialogues.text: His wish was to travel and see the outside world... It's just a shame that I couldn't have been the one to help him.

dialogues.speaker: Aoi
dialogues.text: Heh, well, would you look at that? I've strayed from the topic. I'm afraid I can't help with this music festival. Tsukumomono Groceries can't do without me right now.

dialogues.speaker: Aoi
dialogues.text: Still, I'm glad to have heard this once more. Thank you so much.

dialogues.speaker: Tomoki
dialogues.text: Absolutely fantastic!

dialogues.speaker: Tomoki
dialogues.text: If not for the way you dress, I'd have suspected that you were from Konda Village yourself. It sounded just like the original!

dialogues.speaker: Tomoki
dialogues.text: Alright, I've decided. I'm heading to this festival. Maybe immersing myself in the music there might give me some new ideas.

dialogues.speaker: Tomoki
dialogues.text: I'll move my food stall over there — not that my skills are the most impressive, but I'm sure I'll add to the atmosphere at least, eh?

dialogues.speaker: Yukio
dialogues.text: Wow. What a brilliant recreation! That said, even I have no clue what this song's called, haha.

dialogues.speaker: Yukio
dialogues.text: A fox-eared customer of ours likes humming this one when she comes over for some ramen. She's one of our VIPs. Came round a few days ago, in fact, or I wouldn't have remembered that song at all.

dialogues.speaker: Yukio
dialogues.text: ...I guess that tells you all you need to know about me and music, eh?

dialogues.speaker: Yukio
dialogues.text: If you're looking for a food stall, I'd recommend you look for Tomoki.

dialogues.speaker: Yukio
dialogues.text: That fellow's got a right adventurous spirit. Even if he isn't a fan of music, he should be interested nonetheless.
